sections.h2: Which county sends the Katy tax bill?
sections.html:
The answer depends on the street address, since Katy reaches into Fort Bend, Harris and Waller counties. Your city of Katy tax is added to your county tax bill, and the city has not accepted tax payments at City Hall since September 1, 2015.

The city's tax page lists the places to pay:

  • Fort Bend County: 22333 Grand Corner Drive, Katy, phone 281-341-3710
  • Harris County: 16715 Clay Road, Houston, phone 713-368-2000
  • Waller County: 900 13th Street, Hempstead, phone 979-921-0060

Appraisals are done by three separate districts, the Fort Bend County Appraisal District (281-344-8623), the Harris County Appraisal District (713-957-7800) and the Waller County Appraisal District (979-921-0060). Not sure which county your address is in? Each district's property search will show it, and any bill you received names the collecting office.

Katy had 28,373 residents in mid-2025 by federal estimate, up 29.7 percent from the 2020 base, on 14.54 square miles of land. Fast change in a city's population is a reason to read each year's value notice instead of assuming last year's number.

sections.h2: What rate did Katy propose for 2026?
sections.html:
The city's 2026 notice proposed a rate of $0.420000 per $100 of valuation, down from $0.425000 for 2025. The notice sets the no-new-revenue rate at $0.407051 and the voter-approval rate at $0.443092, and it announced a public hearing for September 28, 2026 at City Hall. Before you rely on the final figure, read the Adopted 2026 Tax Rate tab on the city's tax information page.

The notice also printed these city figures for the average residence homestead:

  • Average homestead taxable value: $383,500 in 2025 and $391,368 in 2026.
  • City tax on the average homestead: $1,629.88 in 2025 and $1,643.75 in 2026.
  • City tax levy on all properties: $25,161,670 in 2025 and $25,729,208 in 2026.

The city share is one slice of the bill. County, school and special district rates share the same statement. The tax formula printed on the notice is the tax rate times the taxable value divided by 100, with exemptions already removed from the taxable value.

sections.h2: How do taxable values compare across the three counties?
sections.html:
They differ sharply. The city's taxpayer impact statement lists the median homestead taxable value in each county portion of Katy.

Median homestead taxable value in Katy by county, from the city's September 2026 taxpayer impact statement
CountyTax year 2025Tax year 2026
Harris County$220,777$223,971
Fort Bend County$433,739$445,946
Waller County$446,196$439,112
Average of the three$366,904$369,676

Federal tables list $401,700 as Katy's middle owner-occupied home value, with 80.7 percent of homes lived in by owners and a middle household income of $114,912. Because roughly four in five Katy homes are owner-occupied, most sellers hold a homestead exemption, and it is worth checking that the record is right before a sale. The same federal page lists 7,942 households of 3.15 people on average, 28.4 percent of residents under 18, and a mean commute of 31.3 minutes.

A seller with tax owed on a Katy house has a plain path. Get the payoff statement from the right county, read the city's adopted rate on its tax page, and tell the title company which of the three counties holds the parcel. The county decides which collector, which appraisal district and which protest board apply, and a wrong guess costs time.

sections.h2: What happens if a Katy tax bill is paid late?
sections.html:
The cutoff is January 31, and the penalty starts February 1: 6 percent plus 1 percent interest, both growing through July. The city's tax page adds a warning that a bill you never received leaves the tax, the due date and the lien exactly where they were.

Each January 1 a lien attaches to the house for that year's tax, which is why a Katy sale cannot close cleanly until the year's bill is settled or credited. Ask the county that bills the address, Fort Bend, Harris or Waller, for a payoff statement, and give it to the title company early.

An owner who fell behind has two tools. A penalty waiver request goes in writing within 181 days of the delinquency date, and a collector may offer a payment plan.

sections.h2: How can a Katy owner lower the bill?
sections.html:
The biggest levers sit with the appraisal district and the exemptions you file for. Because Katy runs through three counties, a Katy owner deals with Fort Bend, Harris or Waller for each of them. These are the main ones:

  • The school district homestead exemption of $140,000, with $60,000 more for seniors and disabled owners.
  • A city or county exemption, if the unit adopted one. Texas lets a unit set up to 20 percent of value with a $5,000 floor, and the Exemption Eligibility tab on Katy's tax page gives the city's terms.
  • The 10 percent yearly limit on homestead value growth, which begins after the exemption is first granted.
  • A protest to the appraisal review board, usually due in mid-May.

A buyer who closes after January 1 can claim the homestead exemption at once for that year when the seller never held it.

sections.h2: How did Katy's 2026 notice describe the rate change?
sections.html:
The notice said the effective rate would rise 0.66 percent, which raises maintenance and operations tax on a $100,000 home by about $2.42. The proposed $0.420000 sits between the no-new-revenue rate of $0.407051 and the voter-approval rate of $0.443092, so no election was required. The notice records every voting council member in favor and none against, with the mayor present and not voting.

A separate taxpayer impact statement for the September 14, 2026 council meeting compares city tax bills on the median homestead: $1,559.34 under the current budget, $1,552.64 under the proposed budget and $1,504.77 at the no-new-revenue rate. These are the city's published estimates for the median homestead, and your own bill depends on your taxable value.

The city sets the rate, but the three appraisal districts set the values. If your value rises while the rate falls, your city bill can still move up.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Katy property tax bill?
sections.html:
Pay the collector for the county where your house sits. Fort Bend County takes online payment by card or electronic check. Its page prints a card fee of 2.29 percent of the total with a $2.75 minimum, no fee for electronic checks, and a 3.95 percent fee on business and international cards. It deposits post-dated checks on receipt, so do not date a check for later.

Questions to the Fort Bend office go to FBCTaxInfo@fortbendcountytx.gov or 281-341-3710. Harris and Waller owners use their own county's collector, as the city page lists. If your lender pays from escrow, look up the account online and confirm the payment posted before January 31.

The city's notice also points owners to Texas.gov/PropertyTaxes, which links to the local property tax database showing proposed rates and hearings for each unit that taxes your address.

faqs.q: Who collects the City of Katy property tax?
faqs.a: Your county's tax office collects it, because the city charge rides on the county bill. Fort Bend, Harris and Waller each have a payment location on the city's tax page.

faqs.q: What rate did Katy propose for 2026?
faqs.a: The notice proposed $0.420000 per $100 of valuation, compared with $0.425000 for 2025. Look at the adopted rate on the city's tax page, then add the county, school and special district rates.

faqs.q: When does Katy tax go delinquent?
faqs.a: After January 31. February 1 brings a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent monthly interest, and bills arrive around October 1.

faqs.q: Does Katy offer its own homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The city's tax page has an Exemption Eligibility tab with its terms. The state school exemption is $140,000 on top of that, with $60,000 more for seniors and disabled owners.

faqs.q: Can I protest my Katy appraisal?
faqs.a: Yes, through the appraisal review board of the county that holds your house. The usual deadline falls in mid-May, or 30 days after a late notice.
